why: Judge B (google/gemini-3.7-flash) shares a vendor with one evaluated model, so assert_cross_vendor blocks that arm. Judge C is vendor-disjoint from all three evaluated models and from judge A, letting one judge pair grade every arm.

outcome.primary_metric_result: THREE-WAY TIE. All three candidates scored boundary kappa 1.000 and success kappa 0.933 with zero judge errors, and all three agreed with judge A at kappa 0.933 on both axes.
outcome.tie_break_applied: measured cost per call (preregistered tie-breaker 2; tie-breaker 1, fewer judge errors, was also tied at 0)

why_the_metric_could_not_discriminate.finding: Every candidate made exactly one error, and it was the same case: question-010/success, where gold is 'achieved' and every judge answered 'not_achieved'.
same_case_missed_by: openai/gpt-5.6-sol (judge A, both the frozen 2026-09-08 run and the 2026-09-09 rerun)
why_the_metric_could_not_discriminate.note: question-010 is the one case where the two human annotators disagreed and blind arbitration moved the gold off the author's seed ('not_achieved' -> 'achieved'). All five judges side with the author's seed and the dissenting annotator. The residual success-axis error is therefore one contested item, not a quality difference between judges.
why_the_metric_could_not_discriminate.consequence: On this 60-case set the success axis is capped at kappa 0.933 for any judge that gets everything else right, so kappa cannot rank these candidates.

judge_a_run_to_run_variance.note: Same model, same fixed judge prompt, and that endpoint accepts no temperature. The rerun reproduced both prior errors and added one, moving success kappa from 0.933 to 0.867. One flipped case at n=30 moves kappa by about 0.07, which is larger than any gap between the three candidates -- there was none.

interpretation_limits: The winner is the maximum of three candidates on the same 60 cases, so its kappa is a selection statistic, optimistically biased, and not an independent validation.
The selection was ultimately made on cost, because measured accuracy was identical. Do not report z-ai/glm-5.3-flash as the most accurate judge.
n=30 per axis, and judge A's rerun shows plus-or-minus one case of run-to-run noise at that n.
These are synthetic constructed cases, not real model outputs. On real outputs the v6 refusal judge scored only kappa 0.737.
Independent validation of judge C requires a fresh held-out batch this selection never touched.

cost_and_throughput.measured_on: the real fixed judge system prompt plus real boundary/success user prompts built from the frozen cases, with OpenRouter usage accounting enabled
